_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning about entrepreneurship — what it means to start a business, and the skills and qualities that help entrepreneurs succeed.

toLevel2.question: An entrepreneur is a person who starts a new business or organisation.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: An entrepreneur identifies an opportunity and takes steps to start something new.

distractors.explanation: Entrepreneurs are people who start businesses; they may also lead or grow them once running.

toLevel2.question: Entrepreneurs need no creative thinking because successful businesses always copy other businesses exactly.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Entrepreneurs typically use creative thinking to find new ideas, products, or ways of doing things.

distractors.explanation: Treating entrepreneurship as pure copying ignores the role of creativity and adaptation in starting a business.

toLevel2.question: Resilience is the ability to keep going through setbacks and challenges.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Resilience helps entrepreneurs continue when their first plan does not work as expected.

distractors.explanation: Resilience covers persistence and adapting after setbacks, both common in entrepreneurship.

toLevel2.question: Problem-solving is unnecessary for entrepreneurs because new businesses never face any unexpected events.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: New businesses regularly face unexpected events, so problem-solving is one of the most useful entrepreneurial skills.

distractors.explanation: Treating new businesses as predictable misses how often entrepreneurs respond to unexpected events.

toLevel2.question: Successful entrepreneurs never take any risk and avoid every uncertain decision.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Starting a new business usually involves some risk; entrepreneurs aim to manage risk, not avoid it entirely.

distractors.explanation: Treating entrepreneurship as risk-free misses how starting a business almost always involves uncertainty.

toLevel2.question: First Nations enterprises in Australia today combine business activity with strong cultural values.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander–owned enterprises bring cultural values into how they operate and what they offer.

distractors.explanation: First Nations enterprises commonly integrate cultural knowledge and values into their business decisions.

toLevel2.question: Entrepreneurs only ever create products and never create services.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Entrepreneurs create both products and services, including tutoring, design, and other service-based work.

distractors.explanation: Restricting entrepreneurship to physical products misses service businesses, which are a large part of the sector.

toLevel2.question: Communication is a useful skill for entrepreneurs when they explain their ideas to customers and partners.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Clear communication helps entrepreneurs reach customers and work with others.

distractors.explanation: Communication is one of the most-cited skills for entrepreneurial success.

toLevel2.question: All entrepreneurs are wealthy adults; young people cannot start businesses of any kind.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Young people can start small businesses, including school-based projects and community-focused ventures.

distractors.explanation: Treating entrepreneurship as adult-only misses the many young entrepreneurs running real businesses.

toLevel2.question: A class business project does not need any decisions about products, customers, or how to make the product.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A class business project typically includes decisions about products, customers, and production methods.

distractors.explanation: Treating these decisions as optional misses the basic planning every business project goes through.

toLevel2.question: Entrepreneurs only succeed in big cities and never in regional or remote communities.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Entrepreneurs run successful businesses in regional and remote communities, including First Nations enterprises on Country.

distractors.explanation: Treating entrepreneurship as a city-only activity misses the many regional and remote success stories across Australia.

toLevel2.question: Entrepreneurs sometimes spot a need in their community and create a product or service to meet it.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Spotting an unmet need is one common starting point for new businesses.

distractors.explanation: Identifying community needs is a typical first step toward starting an enterprise.

toLevel2.correctExplanation: An entrepreneur is someone who starts a new business or organisation, usually by spotting an opportunity.

distractors.answer: A person who refuses to make any decisions about money in
distractors.explanation: Entrepreneurs make many decisions, including financial ones, when starting a business.

distractors.answer: A person who only works as an employee for someone else

distractors.answer: Refusing to listen to feedback from any customer
distractors.explanation: Refusing customer feedback runs counter to the listening skills entrepreneurs typically rely on.

distractors.answer: To avoid every decision until the future is fully clear
distractors.explanation: Avoiding every decision is the opposite of taking a risk.

distractors.answer: A guarantee that every business idea will succeed first time in

toLevel3.question: An entrepreneur who fails one project must immediately give up on entrepreneurship for life.

toLevel3.correctExplanation: Many entrepreneurs adjust after a project ends and try again with new ideas.
